subject: SLA: monthly credit cap and latency SLO carve-out request
messages:
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jose Santos <j.santos@brightwave.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@brightwave.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: SLA template + latency carve-out request

Jose / BrightWave procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. As requested, attaching our standard SLA template and a short note on how we calculate monthly service credits. High level proposal from our side:

- Uptime: 99.95% standard for Hosted API; 99.99% for Dedicated instances (per calendar month).
- Latency: we publish median/95th metrics per route; for Dedicated we propose a 95th percentile P95 <= 300ms target for inference-only endpoints. Hosted latency may vary based on burst patterns.
- Service credit formula: 5% of monthly invoice for each 0.1% below SLA up to a cap of 30% of monthly recurring charges. Credits issued per qualifying incident following an internal verification and claim window.

I know you asked about a specific latency SLO for your mission-critical endpoint and a lower credit cap. We can discuss an exception pathway: a time-boxed pilot where we agree on a supported latency SLO and a temporary adjusted credit cap while we tune routing and batching.

Attachments: SLA_Template_Redlines_v1.docx, Service_Credit_Calculation.xlsx (summary tab).

Next steps: please confirm which of our suggestions you'd like redlined (uptime, credit formula, latency target) and whether your legal team wants a tracked-doc. I'll loop in Lauren from Legal and Aditya (SE) to help with technical specifics.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Jose Santos <j.santos@brightwave.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightwave.com>, BrightWave Technical PM <m.choi@brightwave.com>
Date: 2025-09-11T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA template + latency carve-out request

Vanessa —

Thanks for the materials. A few points from procurement and our engineering lead:

1) Uptime: 99.9% is what procurement typically accepts for SaaS APIs; we're willing to consider higher for Dedicated but need that written into the contract with measurement details.
2) Credits: the 30% cap seems high to us; would you be able to cap at 25%? Also we require credits to be calculated per incident and applied to the following billing cycle.
3) Latency: for our mission-critical ingestion endpoint we need P95 <= 250ms. If Redwood can commit to that for Dedicated instances, we can accept a higher uptime number.
4) Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows should be defined and limited.

Can Lauren or legal send a redline and clarity on definitions (downtime calculation, incident classification)? We prefer to get the SLA language into DocuSign next week if possible.

Regards,
Jose Santos
VP Finance & Ops (acting)
BrightWave
j.santos@brightwave.com

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-12T15:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: SLA template + latency carve-out request

Forwarding Jose's reply — asking for legal + SE input. My read / suggested compromise:

- Offer: Hosted API 99.95% (as standard). Dedicated: 99.99% availability. We can accept a customer-requested lower latency SLO (P95 250ms) for a single Dedicated cluster if they commit to a minimum reserved capacity (1.5x expected peak).
- Credits: move to a per-incident calculation, keep 5% per 0.1% below SLA but cap at 30% standard. For this named exception we can propose a temporary cap of 25% or 30% depending on whether they sign a 12-month committed capacity addendum.
- Maintenance: exclude scheduled maintenance with 48h notice and not to exceed 4 hours/month (we should allow longer for major upgrades with agreed windows).

Aditya — can you confirm feasibility of P95 250ms for Dedicated under reserved capacity and any prerequisites (batching config, model quantization, region placement)? Lauren — can you generate a redline with definitions for "Downtime," "Incident," and "Measurement windows" so procurement can review?

Thanks,
Vanessa

Jose / BrightWave legal —

Attached: SLA_Template_Redlines_v2.docx — key changes summarized below:

- Definitions: clarified measurement methodology (UTC month, 1-minute sampling, service-level window excludes scheduled maintenance and force majeure).
- Credits: changed to per-incident credit calculation; claimant must submit a claim within 14 days of incident end. Credits will be applied to next invoice.
- Credit cap: left at 30% for standard contracts; included a clause allowing the sales team to approve a temporary, documented deviation for pilots or committed-capacity purchases.
- Latency: added a section for "Named Endpoint SLOs" under which parties can list mission-critical routes and agreed P95 latency targets; breach of endpoint SLOs will be accounted separately from platform availability.

We kept the DocuSign-ready language generic but included placeholders for a "Dedicated Capacity Addendum" (if you want a 99.99% pledge and a guaranteed P95 latency).

If you want us to push a DocuSign envelope, confirm signatories and whether you need a PO number.

Regards,

Date: 2025-09-16T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA template + latency carve-out request (BrightWave counterproposal)

Lauren / Vanessa —

Thanks for the redline. BrightWave counterproposal summarized:

- Uptime: Accept Hosted 99.95%. For Dedicated we request 99.99% (we will sign 12-month commit if this is guaranteed).
- Latency (Named Endpoint): Require P95 <= 250ms for the ingestion endpoint. If Redwood requires reserved capacity to meet this target, we will commit to a 1-year reserved capacity agreement and a minimum committed QPS.
- Credit cap: reduce to 25% (applies per month). Credits to be calculated per incident, applied to next invoice, and the buyer must submit claims within 7 days of incident close.
- Maintenance: scheduled maintenance not to exceed 4 hours/month for Dedicated clusters; emergency maintenance should be communicated within 4 hours.

We'll accept a pilot period to demonstrate the 250ms P95, but procurement insists on the 7-day claim window if an SLA breach occurs during the pilot.

Please advise if Redwood can accept the 25% cap and 7-day claim window in exchange for a 12-month committed Dedicated purchase.

Regards,
Jose Santos
BrightWave

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jose Santos <j.santos@brightwave.com>

Date: 2025-09-17T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA template + latency carve-out request (BrightWave counterproposal)

Jose —

Appreciate the clear counterproposal. Quick summary of what Redwood can commit to and the conditional exception we can offer for your ingestion endpoint pilot: 

1) Uptime: we accept your ask — Hosted 99.95% standard; Dedicated 99.99% if BrightWave signs a 12-month reserved capacity addendum.
2) Latency: we can target P95 <= 250ms for the named ingestion endpoint on a Dedicated cluster provided BrightWave commits to reserved capacity (we'll outline the minimum QPS and instance sizing in the Dedicated Addendum). Aditya confirms this is technically feasible with the requested commit and a one-week tuning window.
3) Credits & claim window: Redwood agrees to per-incident credits and application to next invoice. For the committed 12-month Dedicated contract we can accept a 25% monthly cap and a 7-day claim window. For a 60-day pilot (no long-term commit) we can offer a temporary cap of 35% and a 14-day claim window to give both teams more runway while we tune.
4) Maintenance: will keep scheduled maintenance <= 4 hours/month for Dedicated clusters; we will provide 48-hour notices for planned maintenance. Emergency maintenance will be communicated ASAP with a post-event RCA.

If that sounds acceptable, we'll prepare the Dedicated Capacity Addendum and a DocuSign envelope with two options: (A) 12-month reserved capacity + 25% cap & 7-day claim window, or (B) 60-day pilot + 35% cap & 14-day claim window. Please confirm which path you prefer and signatory details; we'll target DocuSign next week.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
